title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
summary: TraceKV replaces full-precision dense KV cache storage for reasoning VLMs with sensitivity-aware low-rank latent representations calibrated on on-policy reasoning states, plus a global rank allocation and custom low-rank attention kernels. It is training-free, but adoption costs integration of on-policy calibration, per-layer rank configuration, and nonstandard attention kernels into the serving stack, with residual accuracy risk from policy drift if calibration diverges from deployment workloads. It can fail when production reasoning traces differ from calibration states, when the target model lacks a supported kernel path, or when stacking with quantization compounds approximation error beyond the near-lossless regime reported.
rationale: The 24 GB GPU constraint makes KV cache reduction directly valuable for long multimodal reasoning contexts, but the method is recent, VLM-specific, and depends on custom kernels and calibration fidelity, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Training-free low-rank KV cache compression for VLMs
